cases.note: readline, tell, seeks from the start, the position and the end, and iteration over lines, in text and in binary.

program.python:
f = open('/data/f.txt')
print(repr(f.readline()), f.tell())
f.seek(0, 2)
print(f.tell())
f.seek(2)
print(repr(f.read(3)))
f.seek(0)
print([line.rstrip() for line in f.readlines()])
f.close()
b = open('/data/f.txt', 'rb')
b.seek(-4, 2)
print(b.read())
b.seek(4)
b.seek(2, 1)
print(b.read(2), b.tell())
b.close()
program.js:
const f = std.open('/data/f.txt', 'r')
console.log(JSON.stringify(f.getline()), f.tell())
f.seek(0, std.SEEK_END)
console.log(f.tell())
f.seek(2, std.SEEK_SET)
console.log(JSON.stringify(f.readAsString(3)))
f.seek(-4, std.SEEK_END)
console.log(JSON.stringify(f.readAsString()))
f.seek(4, std.SEEK_SET)
f.seek(2, std.SEEK_CUR)
console.log(f.getByte(), f.tell())
f.seek(0, std.SEEK_END)
console.log(f.getByte(), f.eof())
f.close()

program.python:
with open('/data/f.txt') as f:
    print(repr(next(f)))
    for line in f:
        print(repr(line))

cases.note: Monty has no os.open; QuickJS's os.seek returns the new offset as a bigint when given one.

program.python:
import os
fd = os.open('/data/f.txt', os.O_RDONLY)
print(os.lseek(fd, -6, os.SEEK_END), os.read(fd, 5))
print(os.lseek(fd, 0, os.SEEK_CUR))
print(os.lseek(fd, 4, os.SEEK_SET), os.read(fd, 3))
print(os.lseek(fd, 1, os.SEEK_CUR), os.read(fd, 100))
os.close(fd)
